properties.name: A release server overflows its 2 MiB worker stack on a reasoning chain about 2,000 steps deep, and the whole process aborts
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-10-25 on a RELEASE build of main 0c567349c (#801 merged), the stack check before cutting 0.92.0. Asked: can the server as shipped overflow its worker stack on a design a person could build? YES.

THREAD STACKS. Every tool call runs on a tokio worker thread. reflow2-mcp uses #[tokio::main] (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs:1517) and never sets thread_stack_size; tokio 1.53.1 leaves the size unset, so each worker gets std's default, 2 MiB (or RUST_MIN_STACK, which neither the Dockerfile nor the flo2.io deployment sets). gdb measured 2 MiB on the overflowing thread. rmcp 3.6.0 spawns each request as a tokio task, so HTTP (--http, --registry-root), stdio and --call (call_over_pipe tokio::spawns the server, main.rs:1241) all run tools on these 2 MiB workers. The 8 MiB main thread only awaits. No rayon pool; spawn_blocking is used only to open a store.

WHAT RECURSES WITH CHAIN DEPTH. (1) foundations_walk, crates/reflow2-core/src/inference.rs:6562, recursive with no depth bound, 528 bytes per frame in release; reached from get_node on any concluded node (tools/query.rs:1708), reasoning.rs:1215, reason_to_exist.rs:314, design_foundations. (2) proof_chain_walk, inference.rs:6914, recursive with no depth bound, about 1,008 bytes per frame; it runs when a claim's top step HOLDS, reached from loop_status and detect_gaps (detect_unconfirmed_reasoning), reasoning_report (reasoning.rs:1645, 1828) and get_node (query.rs:1721). Because #801 shares one memo across a report and conclusions are read in id order, a holding chain's truth is carried past INFERENCE_DEPTH, so this walk does reach the full depth. (3) The truth evaluation itself (truth_full / step_reading / node_reading / objections_within) IS bounded by INFERENCE_DEPTH = 64 (inference.rs:146); its frames are 1-3.4 KB each, fine on 2 MiB in release, and the reason a DEBUG build overflows at 56. closure.rs:634 and report.rs:1705 are bounded at 64; graphalg (scc, cycles, cuts) already uses explicit work stacks.

DEPTH AND TIME (laptop, 4 cores; HTTP on --ephemeral --http, import_graph then the call; one fresh server per design):
- Linear chain, ground does not hold: depth 56 reasoning_report 0.13 s, loop_status 0.16 s, closure_report 0.53 s, get_node 0.02 s. Depth 200: 7.7 / 0.79 / 3.2 / 0.09 s. Depth 1,000: 43.3 / 22.3 / 21.1 / 0.15 s. Depth 3,000 get_node ok 0.33 s. Depth 4,000 get_node OVERFLOW in 1.5 s ("thread 'tokio-rt-worker' has overflowed its stack", exit 134, gdb: about 3,880 foundations_walk frames). Depth 5,000: reasoning_report 199.8 s ok (capped at 500 records), closure_report 131 s ok, loop_status no reply within the 300 s the HTTP stream stays open (on ajs77 through --call it finished in 943.5 s), get_node OVERFLOW 1.5 s.
- Same chain with a ground that holds (every step holds): loop_status depth 1,000 12.5 s ok, 1,500 27.1 s ok, 1,800 42.7 s ok, 1,900 45.5 s ok, 2,000 OVERFLOW after 25 s (gdb: about 2,000 proof_chain_walk frames under loop_status_for > open_questions_for > detect_gaps > all_gaps > detect_unconfirmed_reasoning), 3,000 OVERFLOW. reasoning_report survived 2,000 and 3,000 (80.7 s, 119.7 s).
- #801's Shop-shaped generator (24 decision steps plus a requirement chain): 56 steps all readers under 1 s; 200 steps reasoning_report and even get_node gave no reply within 300 s (server alive, still computing); 1,000 get_node no reply in 300 s; 5,000 get_node OVERFLOW in 1.4 s. On ajs77 through --call the 1,000- and 5,000-step whole-design readers were still computing after 20-36 minutes and were stopped.
- --call on an on-disk (RocksDB) store: get_node at depth 4,000 'fatal runtime error: stack overflow', exit 134; depth 3,000 ok.
- DISCRIMINATING: the same depth-4,000 get_node with RUST_MIN_STACK=8 MiB succeeds (1.6 s), so the limit is the 2 MiB worker stack against an unbounded walk, not a bad record.

CONSEQUENCE. A stack overflow aborts the PROCESS, not the request. On flo2.io one engine process serves every hosted design from one registry root, so one design with a holding chain about 2,000 steps deep, read by loop_status or detect_gaps, or any chain about 3,900 deep read by get_node, takes the engine down for every person on that box. Separately, and earlier than the stack: reading time grows much faster than depth (Shop-shaped 200 steps already past 300 s), far past the gateway's 30 s.

NOT ESTABLISHED: the exact overflow depth on the hosted RocksDB build (leaf frames differ slightly; the walk frames are the same code); whether the Shop-shaped whole-design readers at 1,000-5,000 steps would overflow before finishing; any change to the code. Nothing was fixed. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
